My most-used transcription tool on Mac, MacWhisper, has released another major update today, adding real-time meeting transcription, significantly improved speaker identification, tighter integration with Apple Intelligence, and a brand-new transcription model. Here are the details.

MacWhisper integrates more deeply with Apple Intelligence

I have previously written about how heavily I rely on MacWhisper, especially in my workflow for producing podcasts.

MacWhisper is one of the earliest AI-powered transcription tools designed for Mac. Since independent developer Jordi Bruin launched it in 2023, it has continued to improve and expand its support for new models, services, and workflows.

These include automatic meeting recording and speaker identification, folder monitoring, system-wide dictation, local and cloud AI models, and integrations with services such as Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, and n8n.

Today, MacWhisper updates to version 15.2, introducing improved speaker identification powered by NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Diarization model, which was announced just a few hours ago.

This also brings us to another major feature of this update: real-time meeting transcription.

This feature has occupied a high position on MacWhisper's public roadmap for some time, and now it has finally arrived — users can follow along in real time during meetings, as well as search, copy, or send the live transcript.

Speaking of actual transcription models, MacWhisper 15.2 has added Alibaba's QWEN3-ASR transcription model, which supports 22 languages, along with tighter integration with Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts on macOS 27.

Now, users running macOS (including those in the European Union) can search transcripts system-wide, open them with Siri, extract text into Shortcuts, and reference the transcript currently on screen within Siri or Apple Intelligence requests.

Finally, MacWhisper 15.2 adds the ability to organise transcripts and meetings into folders and subfolders, and supports dragging and dropping existing transcripts into them from the sidebar.
